question: to the Commission Michele Picaro (ECR) Subject:
Revision of Regulation (EU) 2020/1201 on Xylella fastidiosa in the light of new scientific evidence

Xylella fastidiosa’s epidemiological picture has changed dramatically since the bacterium was first detected in Europe more than a decade ago. Monitoring efforts in the EU have identified a number of Xylella subspecies and genotypes which attack different host plants and are characterised by a range of aggression and risk profiles. An example is the situation in Italy, where the impact of certain Xylella fastidiosa variants on agriculture is minor – if not downright negligible – compared to the devastation wrought on the Salento area’s olive crops by subspecies pauca Sequence Type 53. Yet the measures implemented under Regulation (EU) 2020/1201 continue to push a one-size-fits-all approach that is not sufficiently tailored to the different subspecies, strains and areas concerned. Given that the Commission gave EFSA until the end of this year to update its risk assessment for Xylella fastidiosa, I ask the Commission: 1.
Will it, in the light of new scientific findings, revise Regulation (EC) No 2020/1201?
Will it adopt measures that are tailored to individual Xylella subspecies and strains, as well as to their established risk profiles?

Is it considering introducing a more flexible model whereby national plant health authorities can, in coordination with the Commission, adopt strategies that are proportionate to the gravity of individual outbreaks and whose economic repercussions do not outweigh the actual plant health risks involved?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.9.2026) The Commission confirms that it mandated the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) to update the risk assessment for Xylella fastidiosa (M-2024-000291). It explicitly requested from EFSA to update the risk assessment by subspecies of Xylella fastidiosa present in the EU, as well as to consider different scenarios and relevant risk reduction options. The output of EFSA in response to this mandate is expected by the end of 2026. On the basis of the information provided by EFSA, the Commission intends to open a discussion with Member States at the Standing Committee on Plants, Animals, Food and Feed as regards the phytosanitary measures implemented under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/12012, including whether these measures can be more closely tailored to the risk profiles of individual subspecies and strains, and whether further flexibility is warranted to allow for measures that are proportionate to the severity of individual outbreaks.
